pr_title: Add swap byte/word/byteword option to modbus sensor
pr_body:
<!--

## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->
A new option SWAP replaces REVERSE_ORDER, however REVERSE_ORDER is
still accepted and silently converted to SWAP=WORD.

Note: REVERSE_ORDER will be removed in a future release.

Old config:
```yaml
modbus:
  sensors:
    - name: "sensor1"
      address: 17
      reverse_order: true
      ...
   - name: "sensor2"
      address: 17
      reverse_order: false
      ...
```

New config:
```yaml
modbus:
  sensors:
    - name: "sensor1"
      address: 17
      swap: word
      ...
   - name: "sensor2"
      address: 17
      swap: none
      ...
```
swap allows none/byte/word/word_byte options.

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
The existing REVERSE_ORDER can only reverse words, it is replaced with
a proper SWAP option that allows byte/word/word-byte swap, to cover the
normal conversions:

![n Keyword](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6185391/116122343-eec94980-a6c1-11eb-8d5d-dd01cf52c8c9.png)

The existing tests have not been touched, but new test have been added to test the new feature 
(making review easier).

issue_context.body:

## The problem
The reverse_order boolean option reverse the order of all registers, but the reversal of the order should be done for two consecutive 16-bit registers (for 32 bits float).
Unfortunately the byte order might differ between manufacturers of Modbus instruments.

Ideally, there should be variables configuration : byte and word swap.
As described https://store.chipkin.com/articles/how-real-floating-point-and-32-bit-data-is-encoded-in-modbus-rtu-messages


## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Configuration -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 2020.12.1
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): Supervisor
- Integration causing this issue: Modbus
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/modbus

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`

type: tcp
host: 192.168.0.20
port: 502
name: S500

#register_type: input

sensors:

Modbus Group H2

Yes, it's a good idea.   Thank you @janiversen 

Idealy, we need 3 differents reverse option : byte swap , word swap and byte and word swap.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13821602/112759211-507a9300-8ff2-11eb-9fae-31d669ed1091.png)

Sorry to hijak, and thanks for your continued development efforts on modbus!
Can someone confirm the syntex for changing the function codes from the default 4 to read single registry and 6 to write a single registry? The title of this issue suggests that you are using 3?

Have a look at the documentation: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/modbus/ apart from that it depends a lot on what you want to achive...all modbus platforms have the possibility to change read type, the modbus integration allows you to write holding register/registers and coil/coils.

> Have a look at the documentation: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/modbus/ apart from that it depends a lot on what you want to achive...all modbus platforms have the possibility to change read type, the modbus integration allows you to write holding register/registers and coil/coils.

Thanks @janiversen moved to https://community.home-assistant.io/t/modbus-custom-function-support/186677/7

Looks like you did not read the doc. The function code are in essence register types e.g. 0x03 is read holding registers and 0x04 is read input registers. So when you configure your sensors/switches in HA you need to choose the correct input_type. Btw. 0x04 is not default that depends on type of platform you configure.

Thank you thank you for your patience with me I was not aware that the function code was related to register type, much appreciated. By changing the register_type to holding (of leaving it default) I was able to generate function code 3 :) If its clear in the documentation then I missed it, apologies.

Ok. I think we're crossing into the protocol details here, so it would be nice to offload to the library. But it could be ok for now.
I agree it is in the grey level. I will make a PR against pymodbus and see if they are willing to accept in for one of their future versions.
